operation_trace.misalignment_title: O4 (free balance-sheet capacity) has no advancing mechanism in the baseline

operation.parameters: New advisory blueprint element addressed to the Board of Governors: a duty that liquidity rules recognize (credit), up to a capped amount, a bank's discount-window borrowing capacity associated with collateral prepositioned at the Fed as a qualifying liquidity source substitutable for HQLA self-insurance. Cap sized per bank as the lesser of an overall ceiling and a multiple of the bank's discount-window borrowing over a specified period. This is a NEW duty.
operation.proposal: Introduce a NEW advisory obligation (addressed to the Authority, per ADR-003, not as operative text) creating an operative mechanism absent from the baseline: within regulatory liquidity requirements, recognized borrowing capacity tied to prepositioned discount-window collateral may be credited, up to a cap, against required HQLA-style self-insurance. The move imports the reform-proposal concept (currently residing only in obligation-empty horizon items) into a live blueprint element so O4 acquires an advancing mechanism. The RECALIBRATE-style cap parameter (lesser of overall ceiling and a multiple of DW borrowing) is stated as a design instruction to the Authority, not fixed here.
operation.rationale: This duty is NEW: the finding establishes that no live, binding element credits borrowing capacity against liquidity requirements; all live elements (frbdw-collateral, frbdw-discount-window, 12-usc-347b) presuppose pledged assets and lendable value only. The gap is squarely O4: balance-sheet capacity is tied up in liquidity self-insurance with no mechanism to free it. Crediting prepositioned-collateral borrowing capacity substitutes revived LOLR functionality for costly self-insurance, directly freeing capacity for lending. The cap constrains moral hazard (O5). Because this creates a genuinely new duty, it cites the evidence motivating the gap.

citations.quote: recognized borrowing capacity could be capped at the lesser of the overall ceiling and some multiple of the bank's discount window borrowing over a specified period of time.

When 25 percent of large banks’ balance sheets are allocated to safe assets—up from roughly 10 percent before the crisis—that necessarily means less lending for mortgages, small businesses, AI hyperscalers, and critical infrastructure.

This timing 
risk can be mitigated by banks identifying ex ante the assets that will be pledged to the discount 
window as collateral and pre-positioning them accordingly.
if they have prepositioned collateral with the Fed, banks should be able to count DW lending capacity in their stress liquidity calculations.

objective_hook.how: Creates the missing advancing mechanism for O4: crediting capped, prepositioned-collateral borrowing capacity against HQLA self-insurance frees balance-sheet capacity currently locked in safe assets for economic-activity lending.

tradeoff.advances: O4 (frees balance-sheet capacity by substituting recognized borrowing capacity for HQLA self-insurance)
tradeoff.costs: O5 (limiting moral hazard — crediting LOLR capacity against self-insurance increases reliance on the central bank, the very dependence post-crisis rules sought to reduce)
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O4 > O5 (O4 fourth, O5 fifth): 'O4 > O5'. The move advances the higher-ranked objective; the cap parameter mitigates the O5 cost consistent with that ordering.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: Draft/manual classification under ADR-008. Applying hierarchy, delegation, applicability, and status controls, the operative baseline does not require the Board of Governors to credit discount-window borrowing capacity against regulatory liquidity requirements. The live statute, Regulation A, and Federal Reserve operational materials govern eligibility, collateralization, security interests, lendable value, and discount-window lending operations; they do not create an offset to HQLA-style self-insurance. The cited reform proposals and horizon material describe or recommend prepositioning and recognition of borrowing capacity, but their nonbinding or proposed status cannot establish an existing duty. The operation therefore adds a substantively new advisory obligation for the Authority and changes the baseline policy position rather than codifying or clarifying an existing requirement. Although it fills the identified O4 mechanism gap in policy terms, its legal/effect classification is change because the required recognition and substitution are absent from the controlling baseline.

cells_touched.actor: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
cells_touched.activity: Recognize, subject to a cap, discount-window borrowing capacity associated with prepositioned collateral as a qualifying liquidity source creditable against regulatory HQLA-style self-insurance requirements.

draft_classification.evidentiary_ceiling_notes: The affirmative support comes from reform-proposal and legislation-horizon sources. Those sources may motivate and design the new duty but cannot establish that the baseline already imposes it. The operative sources cited for comparison establish collateral and lending mechanics only, not regulatory-liquidity credit.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: O5 (limit moral hazard) served only by proposal-stage caps, not by live obligations

operation.parameters: Advisory blueprint recommendation addressed to the Board of Governors: create a NEW live operative obligation that conditions any LOLR access-expansion (e.g., recognition within liquidity rules of prepositioned discount-window borrowing capacity) on a countervailing moral-hazard-limiting condition — namely a per-bank recognized-borrowing-capacity cap, sized as the lesser of an overall ceiling and a multiple of the bank's discount window borrowing over a specified period. The obligation would live within the Board's rulemaking authority over discount-window/liquidity treatment, not as a proposal-stage aspiration.
operation.proposal: Advise the Board of Governors to convert the currently proposal-only 'recognized borrowing capacity' cap into a live, binding condition attached to any expansion of LOLR/discount-window recognition: access-expansion may be granted only where a recognized-borrowing-capacity cap is operative for the institution. This is a NEW duty — no existing operative element ties LOLR access-expansion to a moral-hazard-limiting condition. Blueprint-level only; the Authority drafts operative text (ADR-003).
operation.rationale: This duty is NEW. The finding establishes that O5 (limit moral hazard) is served only at the proposal stage (mckernan-reset-liquidity OP-048 has no operative obligation) while the insolvency and undercapitalized-institution limits (12-usc-343, 12-cfr-201-reg-a, 12-usc-347b) serve credit-risk/taxpayer protection and contribute to O5 only incidentally. Making the recognized-borrowing-capacity cap a live condition on access-expansion supplies the missing live O5 instrument, bounding reliance on LOLR as access is broadened. The evidence motivating the gap is the source's own account of moral-hazard concern and the proposed cap's design. Directed to the Board, which already holds prescribing authority over discount-window terms.

citations.quote: recognized borrowing capacity could be capped at the lesser of the overall ceiling and some multiple of the bank's discount window borrowing over a specified period of time.
reflect[s] a desire to reduce dependence on the central bank as a lender of last resort (LOLR)

All such discounts for any participant in any program or facility with broad-based eligibility shall be subject to such limitations, restrictions, and regulations as the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System may prescribe.

objective_hook.how: Supplies the missing live O5 instrument: a binding recognized-borrowing-capacity cap that bounds each bank's reliance on LOLR, limiting the moral hazard that expanded discount-window access would otherwise create.

tradeoff.costs: O4 (free up balance-sheet capacity by expanding recognized LOLR-backed capacity)
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O4 > O5 (O1 > O2 > O3 > O4 > O5); the cap must therefore be calibrated not to negate the O4 gains it conditions — O4 takes precedence over O5 where they conflict.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative baseline does not require the proposed condition. The cited reform proposal describes a recognized-borrowing-capacity cap, but its proposal status cannot establish a live duty. The operative authorities addressing insolvent or undercapitalized borrowing constrain access for credit-risk and taxpayer-protection purposes; they do not require the Board to condition every expansion of LOLR or discount-window recognition on an institution-specific moral-hazard cap. Section 12 U.S.C. § 343 authorizes the Board to prescribe limitations, restrictions, and regulations, but delegated rulemaking authority is not itself an obligation to adopt this particular cap. The operation would therefore create a new binding condition and alter the legal baseline rather than codify or clarify an existing requirement. Its draft effect class is change, subject to human confirmation under the disclosed manual-classification posture.

operation.proposal: Advise the Board to relate the new recognized-borrowing-capacity cap to its existing authority under 12-usc-343 OBL-5 (and its Regulation A prescribing powers), so the moral-hazard-limiting cap is understood as a prescribed limitation on access rather than an unanchored new regime.
operation.rationale: Anchoring avoids creating a duplicative or orphaned instrument: the Board already 'may prescribe' limitations and restrictions on discount access. Relating the O5 cap to that authority clarifies the legal seat of the live obligation proposed in op 1 and shows the cap is a limitation ON access-expansion, keeping the O5 condition tethered to the access it bounds.

objective_hook.how: Secures the O5 instrument by tying the moral-hazard-limiting cap to the Board's existing authority to prescribe limitations on discount access, ensuring the condition is operative and enforceable rather than proposal-stage.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative statutory baseline in 12 U.S.C. § 343 authorizes the Board to prescribe limitations, restrictions, and regulations for broad-based discount programs, but it does not require a recognized-borrowing-capacity cap or require the Board to characterize such a cap as a § 343 limitation. The cited delegation therefore supplies a possible legal seat for the proposed obligation without itself establishing that obligation. The proposed relationship is also expressly contingent on a separate operation introducing the cap as a live requirement. Because the cap currently appears only in a reform proposal, status controls and evidentiary ceilings prevent treating it as part of the operative baseline. Relating a newly operative moral-hazard cap to existing prescribing authority would consequently alter the current duty structure rather than merely clarify or codify it. The operation is workable as a change, but it cannot independently fill M1 unless the antecedent operation making the cap live is adopted.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: O3 (revived Fed LOLR, reduced contagion) advanced only through fragile guidance-level readiness duties

operation.parameters: Addressed to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (as the Authority with rulemaking power under 12 USC 347b/343). Advisory blueprint recommendation to promulgate a binding rule requiring covered depository institutions above a size/less-stable-funding threshold to establish and maintain discount-window operational readiness (executed borrowing arrangements, pre-positioned collateral sized to a defined fraction of runnable liabilities, and periodic test transactions), converting the current 'should' guidance in cfp-addendum-2023 ob-9/ob-10 and occ-bulletin-2023-25 O1 into an enforceable duty.
operation.proposal: Recommend that the Board introduce a NEW binding operational-readiness obligation: covered institutions must (not 'should') establish executed discount-window borrowing arrangements, pre-position collateral in an amount appropriate to potential contingency funding needs, and periodically test access. This elevates the guidance-level readiness expectations into a designed, enforceable component of the LOLR-revival mechanism. This duty is NEW: current instruments state only that institutions 'should' maintain readiness and only 'if the discount window is a part of' their plans.
operation.rationale: The finding establishes that O3's core mechanism — members actually able to reach the discount window quickly in a rapid run — currently rests only on 'should'/'conditional' guidance, so readiness is not assured when a fast run hits. A binding readiness rule makes the LOLR revival a designed mechanism rather than an aspirational assemblage. The duty is NEW: the cited instruments impose no mandatory readiness obligation. Under ADR-003 this is an advisory blueprint move addressed to the Board, not operative text; the Board's authority to prescribe rules governing advances is the vehicle.

citations.quote: If the discount window is a part of a depository institution's contingency funding plans, the depository institution should establish and maintain operational readiness to borrow from the discount window.

understand requirements and maintain operational readiness to borrow from federal funding facilities, such as the Federal Reserve discount window, if these facilities are part of their contingency funding plans.

Any Federal Reserve bank, under rules and regulations prescribed by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, may make advances to any member bank on its time or demand notes having maturities of not more than four months and which are secured to the satisfaction of such Federal Reserve bank.

objective_hook.how: Converts the guidance-level readiness expectation into a binding duty so that members are actually able to reach the discount window quickly in a rapid run, making the revived Fed LOLR functionality a designed mechanism that reduces contagion rather than an aspirational hope.

tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O3 > O4 ('O3 > O4'): mandatory pre-positioned collateral and executed arrangements re-tie some balance-sheet capacity to liquidity self-insurance (O4 cost), but O3 outranks O4, so the readiness gain is preferred.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The applicable baseline does not already require the proposed output. At the statutory level, 12 USC 347b delegates rulemaking authority to the Board and permits Federal Reserve Banks to make qualifying advances, but its operative term is “may”; it does not require depository institutions to execute borrowing arrangements, pre-position collateral, or conduct test transactions. The cited CFP Addendum and OCC Bulletin are supervisory guidance using “should” and conditioning readiness on the discount window being part of an institution’s contingency funding plan. Their status and language cannot establish a universally binding readiness duty. The FHFA policy-report coordination expectations likewise do not impose enforceable obligations on covered depository institutions. The operation would add mandatory conduct, coverage thresholds, collateral-sizing requirements, and periodic testing where the baseline supplies only authority and nonbinding or conditional expectations. It therefore changes the legal baseline rather than codifying or clarifying an existing duty. This remains an advisory recommendation to the Board unless and until the Board promulgates a valid binding rule through the required process.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: O3 (revived Fed LOLR, reduced contagion) advanced only through fragile guidance-level readiness duties

operation.parameters: Addressed to the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (and, jointly, FHFA) as the Authorities. Advisory recommendation to establish binding standing collateral-transfer arrangements between the regional Federal Reserve Banks and the FHLBanks so that when a member's activity must move from FHLBank advances to the discount window, expedited collateral movement is assured by rule rather than by 'expects'/'conditional' coordination language.
operation.proposal: Recommend a NEW binding coordination obligation converting fhfa-system-at-100 OB-5's 'FHFA expects the FHLBanks to negotiate' collateral-transfer arrangements into a mandatory, pre-established standing protocol between Federal Reserve Banks and FHLBanks for expedited collateral movement in a run. This closes the OP-072/OP-113 dependency chain identified in the finding, so the FHLB-to-Fed transition is an enforceable pathway. This duty is NEW: the source expresses only an expectation in a policy report.
operation.rationale: The finding names the FHLB-to-Fed transition and collateral-transfer arrangements as 'conditional'/'should' expectations in a policy_report, not enforceable obligations. In a fast run the transition from FHLBank advances (which withdraw from troubled members) to the discount window is exactly where contagion propagates; without a binding standing protocol, collateral cannot move fast enough. A mandatory pre-established arrangement makes the transition a designed part of the LOLR mechanism. The duty is NEW. ADR-003: advisory, addressed to the Fed/FHFA, no operative text drafted.

citations.quote: Additionally, FHFA expects the FHLBanks to negotiate appropriate agreements with the regional Federal Reserve Banks to ensure expedited movement of collateral if a member's lending activity must be moved to the Federal Reserve discount window.

The FHLBanks can better serve their members if they coordinate with their large depository institution members and the members' prudential regulators to make certain that these members have established protocols to meet their emergency liquidity needs from the Federal Reserve discount window when necessary.

objective_hook.how: Makes the FHLB-to-Fed collateral-transfer transition an enforceable standing arrangement, directly reviving Fed LOLR functionality and reducing contagion risk when FHLBank advances are withdrawn from a stressed member in a rapid run.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The baseline does not already require the proposed output. FHFA-system-at-100 states that FHFA “expects” FHLBanks to negotiate agreements and describes coordination that would improve emergency-liquidity preparedness; as a policy report, this language is advisory and does not create a binding duty for FHFA, the Board of Governors, regional Federal Reserve Banks, or FHLBanks. The cited discount-window statutes provide permissive authority (“may”) rather than mandating standing collateral-transfer arrangements. Guidance-level readiness expectations elsewhere cannot be elevated into enforceable interagency obligations, particularly against actors outside their operative scope. The operation would therefore use existing authority to impose a new mandatory, pre-established protocol governing expedited collateral movement and the FHLB-to-Fed transition. It changes the deontic status from expected or recommended coordination to a binding obligation and is properly classified as change, not codify, clarify, or fill_gap.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: O1 (confidence under fast-run conditions) depends on stigma-mitigation content that exists only as diagnostic vocabulary

operation.parameters: New advisory blueprint duty addressed to the Federal Reserve Board: establish a mandatory periodic discount-window test-borrowing obligation for eligible depository institutions, calibrated by size tier (e.g., large institutions quarterly, mid-size semi-annual), so that routine window use is normalized and stigma is suppressed by design. Advisory only per ADR-003 — the Authority drafts operative text.
operation.proposal: Introduce a NEW live obligation (currently absent) requiring in-scope depository institutions to conduct routine test borrowing at the discount window on a fixed cadence. The move converts 'discount-window stigma' from diagnostic vocabulary into a confidence-preserving mechanism: if all comparable banks borrow routinely, a single bank's borrowing no longer signals weakness. Cadence tiers and the eligibility line are to be set by the Board; this proposal supplies the design intent, not the numeric text.
operation.rationale: This duty is NEW. The finding records that stigma-mitigation exists only as defined vocabulary with no operative obligation. The Warner-Kennedy blueprint evidences the design (mandatory test borrowing by tier) and the stigma-normalization theory ('Having DW access should be no more stigmatizing than having deposit insurance'). Routine, universal testing breaks the 'if you only go to the window when things are really bad, then going to the window signals that things are really bad' dynamic that entrenches stigma.

citations.quote: Mandates that eligible depository institutions operating in the United States engage in test borrowing at the Federal Reserve’s Discount Window:
reduce the unnecessary stigma associated with that use

Since the 2008 financial 
crisis, banks have worried that news of their borrowing from the discount window could be 
perceived as a sign of weakness, thereby exacerbating a run.

objective_hook.how: O1 under fast-run conditions turns on institutions drawing before confidence collapses. A mandatory routine-testing duty normalizes window use so borrowing no longer signals weakness, directly preserving confidence during a fast run rather than leaving it to drafting accident.

tradeoff.advances: O1 (confidence under fast-run conditions) and O3 (revived LOLR functionality / reduced contagion)
tradeoff.costs: O5 (moral hazard) — normalizing routine window reliance may reduce banks' incentive to self-insure liquidity risk
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O1 > O5 (and O3 > O5): 'RANKING (highest first): O1 > O2 > O3 > O4 > O5'. Confidence-preservation and LOLR revival outrank moral-hazard limitation, so the tradeoff resolves in favor of the move.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative baseline does not require periodic discount-window test borrowing. Although 12 CFR part 201 governs Federal Reserve credit and establishes discount-window eligibility and terms, no identified provision imposes fixed-cadence test borrowing on eligible depository institutions or directs the Board to create such a program. The cited Hsu material describes stigma as a diagnostic problem but does not create a binding duty. The Warner-Kennedy modernization item supplies a proposed mandate and design rationale, not currently operative law; it therefore cannot establish the baseline obligation. Applicability would also need to be newly specified by the Board through eligibility and size-tier rules. Because the operation adds affirmative conduct, cadence, and implementation duties absent from controlling authority, it changes the baseline rather than codifying or clarifying it. The advisory posture does not alter that effect classification: if adopted as operative text by the Authority, the output would create a new legal obligation.

operation.parameters: Canonicalize 'discount-window stigma' as an operative defined term within Regulation A's definitions (§ 201.2 scope), drawing the substance from the Hsu formulation, so downstream operative duties (the test-borrowing obligation above) have a stable anchor.
operation.proposal: Elevate 'discount-window stigma' from scattered diagnostic usage across guidance items into a single canonical defined term sited in the operative Regulation A framework, defined as the phenomenon whereby banks fear that news of their window borrowing signals weakness and exacerbates a run. This gives the new test-borrowing duty and any disclosure-timing rule a determinate object to suppress.
operation.rationale: The finding is that stigma exists 'only as diagnostic vocabulary' across four items with no operative home. Canonicalizing the term in the operative regulation is the definitional predicate for the INTRODUCE move; without a defined operative target, the stigma-suppression duty floats. The term is defined verbatim in Hsu; the other items use it undefined.

objective_hook.how: Serves O1 by giving the stigma-suppression design a determinate, operative referent so confidence-preserving duties can attach to it rather than remaining diagnostic prose.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The baseline does not already require Regulation A to define “discount-window stigma” or impose a duty directed at suppressing it. Section 201.2 supplies operative definitions for Regulation A, but the supplied record identifies no existing statutory or regulatory definition of this term, no superior-law command to adopt one, and no delegated gap whose completion is legally compelled. The Hsu and McKernan formulations describe the phenomenon diagnostically; they do not establish a binding definition or regulated-party obligation. References in reform, modernization, or guidance materials likewise cannot elevate the concept into the operative regulatory baseline. Adding the term to Regulation A would therefore alter the codified framework and potentially affect the construction of downstream test-borrowing or disclosure duties. It is not merely codification or clarification of an existing requirement. Although the definition alone would not suppress stigma or cure M5, its insertion is a change to the operative baseline and is meaningful principally when composed with a separately introduced duty.

operation.parameters: Adjust the stress-cadence trigger: rather than the Board's discretionary 'may temporarily require ... more frequent' power for monthly filers, establish a defined continuous/near-real-time reporting escalation that activates on objective fast-run indicators, closing the detection-latency gap the OP-089/OP-112 cadence cluster exposes.
operation.proposal: Recalibrate the FR 2052a stress-frequency mechanism from a discretionary temporary uplift into a pre-committed escalation to continuous (intraday/daily) submission triggered by defined fast-run signals, so detection does not lag behind hours-scale runs. The specific trigger metric and cadence are for the Board to set; this proposal fixes the escalation as automatic rather than ad hoc.
operation.rationale: The finding records that fast-run detection rests on FR 2052a cadence (daily/monthly) and quarterly Call Reports with 'no continuous detection mechanism.' The existing OB-5 power is discretionary and slow. Recalibrating the applicability line/frequency of the stress trigger addresses the latency directly. Confidence (O1) cannot be preserved if a run is detected only after the cadence window passes.

citations.quote: Consistent with current supervisory authority and processes, the Board, during periods of stress, may temporarily require FR 2052a liquidity data from monthly filers on a more frequent basis.

The data provided in the FR 
2052a report meets this need.

objective_hook.how: Serves O1: confidence under fast-run conditions requires detecting the run within its hours-scale window. Converting discretionary temporary uplift into an automatic continuous-reporting escalation closes the detection-latency gap so intervention can precede confidence collapse.

tradeoff.advances: O1 (fast-run detection supporting confidence) and O3 (earlier LOLR deployment)
tradeoff.costs: O4 (balance-sheet capacity) — heavier continuous reporting imposes operational burden that ties up resources
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O1 > O4 and O3 > O4: 'O1 > O2 > O3 > O4 > O5'. Detection serving confidence and LOLR outranks the reporting-burden cost to balance-sheet capacity.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The operative FR 2052a baseline gives the Board discretionary authority during periods of stress to temporarily require more frequent reporting from monthly filers: it says the Board “may” do so. That language neither requires the Board to escalate automatically nor creates an objective fast-run trigger, continuous or intraday submission duty, or precommitted cadence. The operation would replace discretion with a mandatory trigger-response mechanism and would alter the timing and applicability of reporting obligations for affected filers. Quarterly Call Report requirements do not supply the missing escalation, and diagnostic vocabulary or reform recommendations concerning fast runs or discount-window stigma cannot establish a binding reporting duty. Accordingly, the output is not codification or clarification of an existing obligation; it changes the operative baseline by creating a new automatic escalation requirement, even though the Board would retain discretion to specify the trigger metrics and exact escalated cadence.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: 12-cfr-1266-advances carries no in-scope obligation and serves no Mandate objective in the baseline

operation.parameters: Remove 12-cfr-1266-advances from the redesign scope; retain, if desired, as an out-of-scope descriptive cross-reference only.
operation.proposal: Advise the Authority to repeal the 12-cfr-1266-advances node from the liquidity-redesign scope. As instantiated it is nothing_in_scope=true with an empty obligations array and empty defined_terms; it functions only as a binding_authority placeholder. Repealing it from scope removes a node that carries no in-scope obligation and advances none of O1-O5, tightening the blueprint to nodes that actually serve the Mandate.
operation.rationale: The finding establishes that this node advances none of O1-O5 as instantiated: it has no obligations, no defined terms, and serves only as a descriptive authority placeholder. Carrying an inert node dilutes the blueprint without serving any ranked objective. Repeal from scope is the minimal move that resolves the misalignment. Note this is a scope repeal (blueprint hygiene), not repeal of the underlying FHFA regulation. operation_trace.misalignment_title: Universal collateralization and lendable-value burden weighs against O4 while advancing O2/O5

operation.parameters: Replace automatic zero-value assignment for securities lacking an external-vendor price with a fallback valuation procedure (model/matrix price with conservative haircut) before defaulting to zero.
operation.proposal: Advise the Board/Reserve Banks to recalibrate the zero-collateral-value rule so that a security whose price is unavailable from external vendors is first eligible for a conservative fallback valuation (e.g., model or matrix pricing with an elevated haircut) and receives zero value only where no defensible value can be established. This reduces automatic zero-value assignments that force institutions to pledge additional assets to cover the same borrowing need.
operation.rationale: The finding identifies zero-value assignments (frbdw-collateral OBL-4/OBL-5) as a distinct driver of over-pledging burden on O4. The zero-value default is an operational valuation choice, not a statutory command; softening it to a conservative-fallback ladder is a threshold/applicability adjustment (RECALIBRATE) that still satisfies the lendable-value duty and taxpayer protection.

citations.quote: Securities for which a price is unavailable from external vendors will receive zero collateral value.

objective_hook.how: Avoiding automatic zero-value on otherwise-good collateral lets institutions realize borrowing capacity from assets they already hold, freeing balance-sheet capacity per O4.

tradeoff.advances: O4 (recognizes value in collateral currently assigned zero)
tradeoff.costs: O2/O5 (valuing hard-to-price assets carries residual taxpayer-loss risk)
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O2 > O4 > O5. Because O2 outranks O4, the fallback valuation must remain 'consistent with sound risk management practices and to ensure protection for the taxpayer'; the conservative haircut requirement is the O2-protective bound within which O4 may be advanced.

The proposed model/matrix-pricing step with a conservative haircut would replace that automatic result with a new valuation pathway and therefore alter, rather than merely explain or codify, the existing rule. Higher-level authorities require assignment of lendable value, sound risk management, adequate collateral, and taxpayer protection, but they do not require the proposed fallback method or negate the stated zero-value rule. Those authorities leave valuation-method discretion to the Board and Reserve Banks; exercising that discretion differently is a permissible recalibration but remains a change to the current baseline. Applicability is limited to otherwise eligible securities for which external-vendor pricing is unavailable, with zero value retained where no defensible fallback value can be established. operation.parameters: Widen the 60-day/120-day applicability line for undercapitalized depository institutions during Board-declared fast-run/systemic-stress conditions: authorize the Board to suspend or extend the 60-day cap on a facility-wide basis for the duration of a declared rapid-run episode, in place of the current per-institution, per-certification renewal mechanic. Advisory to the Board of Governors under 12 USC 347b(a)/(b); no operative text drafted.
operation.proposal: Advise the Board to recalibrate the 60-days-in-any-120-day limitation (347b-4) so that, upon a Board declaration of fast-run/systemic-stress conditions, the applicability line shifts: the standard cap is suspended or lengthened for undercapitalized members for the declared episode, rather than requiring the slower single-institution viability-certification renewals of 347b-5. This keeps LOLR support flowing to the very institutions whose failure most threatens contagion, precisely when runs are fastest.
operation.rationale: The finding shows O1 (confidence) and O3 (survival/contagion) rank above O2 (avoid bailouts) and O5 (moral hazard), yet the 60/120-day cap withdraws support from the weakest members exactly when their failure most threatens confidence and spreads contagion. RECALIBRATE adjusts the applicability line/frequency without repealing the underlying prudential structure — the viability certification path (347b-5) and the no-obligation-to-lend backstop (347b-4 exception, 347b para (4)) remain. This is a threshold/applicability recalibration under change-class governance, not a free-form edit.

citations.quote: Except as provided in paragraph (2), no advances to any undercapitalized depository institution by any Federal Reserve bank under this section may be outstanding for more than 60 days in any 120-day period.
the limitation contained in paragraph (1) shall not apply during the 60-day period beginning on the date such certification is received.

objective_hook.how: Extending LOLR availability to undercapitalized members during declared rapid-run episodes directly improves their survival odds and reduces contagion (O3), and by preventing visible withdrawal of support from marginal members it sustains systemic confidence (O1) — the two highest-ranked objectives implicated.

tradeoff.advances: O1 (confidence) and O3 (survival/reduce contagion) — sustaining LOLR to weak members in fast runs
tradeoff.costs: O2 (avoid bailouts) and O5 (limit moral hazard) — extended support to undercapitalized institutions increases bailout exposure and weakens market discipline
tradeoff.ranking_basis: Mandate ranks O1 > O2 > O3 > O4 > O5. O1 outranks both O2 and O5; O3 outranks O5 but O3 is below O2. The advance/cost pair O1&O3 vs O2&O5: O1 (advanced) outranks O2 (cost), so the highest-ranked objective in play favors the move; the O3-vs-O2 sub-pair is inverted (O2 > O3). Because the pair is ranked (O1 dominates), ranking_basis is stated, but the O3<O2 tension is flagged for Principal attention.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The controlling statutory baseline, 12 U.S.C. § 347b, expressly limits Federal Reserve Bank advances to an undercapitalized depository institution to 60 days in any 120-day period, subject to the statute’s specified certification-based exception. The proposed facility-wide suspension or extension during Board-declared fast-run/systemic-stress conditions would create a new exception and replace the existing institution-specific certification mechanism for the declared episode. Nothing in the cited text delegates to the Board authority to waive or lengthen the statutory limit based solely on a systemic-stress declaration. Regulation A cannot override or enlarge the Board’s authority beyond that statute. The no-obligation-to-lend provision preserves Reserve Bank discretion not to lend; it does not authorize lending contrary to the duration cap. Accordingly, the baseline does not already require or permit the proposed output, and implementing it would alter the governing applicability and duration rule rather than codify, clarify, or fill a delegated gap. Although styled as advisory recalibration, the substantive result requires a statutory change or other independently established authority.

The FHFA System at 100 report supports coordination and negotiated protocols for transitioning emergency liquidity to the Federal Reserve, but it does not establish that existing law already requires the stock lien to yield. An agreement-negotiation expectation cannot, without sufficient delegated authority and operative legal terms, be read as already requiring FHLBanks to surrender or subordinate statutory protection. The proposed duty therefore changes the baseline by adding a specific pre-cleared release/subordination obligation and reallocating priority between FHLBanks and Reserve Banks. Implementation may require congressional amendment or other valid statutory authorization; FHFA could advise Congress and pursue agreements within its authority, but the cited sources do not establish that FHFA may unilaterally override § 1430’s priority rule. operation.parameters: Advisory blueprint recommendation to the Board of Governors: introduce a NEW purpose-statement element, addressed to the Authority, that names bailout-avoidance as the design objective governing the aggregate of the §13(3) constraints (broad-based-eligibility, single-company prohibition, insolvency prohibition, Treasury approval, reporting/termination), so that the policies-and-procedures regulation the Board must establish declares avoidance-of-bailouts as its organizing purpose rather than leaving it as an incidental aggregate effect.
operation.proposal: Add a new named-purpose element at the head of the emergency-lending policies-and-procedures regime the Board is already required to establish (OBL-6), stating that the collected constraints exist to avoid bailouts of failing firms while preserving system-wide liquidity provision. This is a NEW duty: it converts the currently-implicit design goal into an explicit governing-purpose element the regulation must articulate and against which the constituent constraints are read. It does not alter any threshold, vote count, or approval requirement; it supplies the missing objective anchor. Advisory only, addressed to the Board (ADR-003).
operation.rationale: The finding (M5) is that O2 emerges only from the aggregate effect of governance/taxpayer-loss controls, with no element naming bailout-avoidance as its purpose. The statute already embeds this purpose in narrative — 'not to aid a failing financial company' — but it sits in the policies-and-procedures design instruction rather than as a declared governing purpose. Introducing an explicit purpose element makes O2 a designed, not incidental, feature, and gives interpreters an anchor for reading the constraint cluster. The duty is NEW; it is motivated by the finding's basis that no element names the objective.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The controlling federal statute applies to the Board of Governors and requires it, by regulation and in consultation with the Treasury Secretary, to establish policies and procedures governing §13(3) emergency lending. It also requires those policies and procedures to be designed to ensure system-wide liquidity provision rather than aid to a failing financial company, taxpayer protection, and timely termination. That substantive design instruction strongly supports bailout avoidance, but it does not require the regulation to contain a separate, named purpose-statement element or expressly label “avoidance of bailouts” as the organizing purpose against which all constraints must be read. The operation therefore adds a new articulation duty to OBL-6 rather than merely restating an already-required regulatory output. Its consistency with the statutory purpose does not make the added form and interpretive function baseline-required. Accordingly, the honest draft classification is change, notwithstanding that the recommendation changes no lending threshold, vote count, or approval requirement.

operation_trace.misalignment_title: O2 (avoid bailouts) advanced chiefly by §13(3) constraints framed as taxpayer-protection drafting rather than a bailout-avoidance design

operation.parameters: Advisory blueprint recommendation: establish an explicit relation binding the broad-based-eligibility authorization (OBL-3), the single-company/failing-firm exclusions (OBL-8 and the §13(3)(A)(iii) exclusion), the insolvency prohibition, and the taxpayer-protection collateral rule (OBL-7) as the coordinated instruments implementing the bailout-avoidance purpose element introduced above.
operation.proposal: Relate the dispersed §13(3) constraints — broad-based eligibility, single-company facility prohibition, insolvency prohibition, and lendable-value/taxpayer-protection collateral rule — to one another as a coherent bailout-avoidance instrument set under the newly named purpose. This makes explicit that these obligations function together toward O2, rather than being read as independent taxpayer-loss or governance controls. Advisory, addressed to the Board; no operative text drafted (ADR-003).
operation.rationale: M5 observes that O2 rests on constraint-drafting whose alignment is incidental because the constraints are scattered and framed individually as emergency-lending governance / taxpayer-loss controls. Relating them as a designed set — anchored to the purpose element in op 1 — makes the bailout-avoidance function legible and auditable, without changing any binding threshold.

citations.quote: to discount for any participant in any program or facility with broad-based eligibility, notes, drafts, and bills of exchange when such notes, drafts, and bills of exchange are indorsed or otherwise secured to the satisfaction of the Federal reserve bank

A program or facility that is structured to remove assets from the balance sheet of a single and specific company, or that is established for the purpose of assisting a single and specific company avoid bankruptcy, resolution under title II of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, or any other Federal or State insolvency proceeding, shall not be considered a program or facility with broad-based eligibility.

The policies and procedures established by the Board shall require that a Federal reserve bank assign, consistent with sound risk management practices and to ensure protection for the taxpayer, a lendable value to all collateral for a loan executed by a Federal reserve bank under this paragraph

operation.composition_note: Depends on op 1: the relation is anchored to the bailout-avoidance purpose element introduced there; without that element there is no named objective to relate the constraints to.

objective_hook.how: Serves O2 by making the constraint cluster a legible, coordinated bailout-avoidance mechanism, curing the M5 defect that O2 alignment is incidental to individually-framed controls.

draft_classification.baseline_reasoning: The statutory baseline in 12 U.S.C. § 343 independently requires broad-based eligibility, excludes facilities directed at a single and specific company, prohibits lending to insolvent borrowers through Board-established procedures, and requires collateral lendable-value practices protecting taxpayers. Regulation A may restate or implement those controls under delegated authority, but neither the cited statutory text nor the described regulatory baseline expressly binds them together as a coordinated instrument set implementing a named bailout-avoidance purpose. The proposed RELATE-OBLIGATION operation would add that purposive and structural relationship, anchored to a new purpose element from operation 1. That relationship may accurately describe an aggregate policy effect, but it is not already required by the controlling text and cannot be treated as mere clarification of an existing express linkage. Because it introduces a new blueprint-level design relation without changing the underlying lending thresholds, exclusions, or collateral duties, it is properly classified as change rather than codify or clarify. Its advisory form and absence of drafted operative text do not make the new relation part of the current legal baseline.

cells_touched.actor: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
cells_touched.activity: Establish an explicit blueprint relationship treating the § 13(3) eligibility, firm-specific assistance, insolvency, and collateral safeguards as a coordinated bailout-avoidance instrument set
Administer § 13(3) emergency-lending constraints under the proposed coordinated bailout-avoidance framing

draft_classification.evidentiary_ceiling_notes: The quoted provisions from 12 U.S.C. § 343 establish the existing individual statutory constraints, but not the proposed purpose-based relationship among them. The operation itself is an advisory blueprint recommendation and therefore cannot establish a binding duty or prove that the current baseline already contains the proposed relation. Its dependency on a separately proposed purpose element likewise supports change classification.

cannot_express_log.note: The whitelist cannot compel Congress to convert the permissive statutory discount-window authority (12 USC 347b/343 'may') into a mandatory Fed lending duty — 12-usc-347b 347b-4(4) affirmatively preserves that 'A Federal Reserve bank shall have no obligation to make... any advance', a statutory feature only Congressional action can alter. This exceeds RECALIBRATE/INTRODUCE at the blueprint level and would require an ADR flagging that the binding-LOLR-supply leg of O3 is unreachable without statutory change; logged as a finding, not an edit.

A needed complementary move — mandating DISCLOSURE-TIMING protections (e.g., delaying or masking public reporting of individual window borrowing so routine draws cannot be reverse-engineered as distress signals) — cannot be cleanly expressed on the whitelist. It is neither a threshold RECALIBRATE nor a standalone INTRODUCE of a duty on a determinate actor without touching the confidentiality/publication regime (FR2052A-OB-6 'Micro data ... are considered confidential and are not published'; Reg-A OBL-7 7-day public-availability duty) in ways that may require balancing statutory transparency obligations. This is logged as a candidate ADR on stigma-disclosure-timing rather than improvised here, since it may implicate a transparency constraint the Mandate has not ranked against O1.

The finding also flags sr-10-6-liquidity-policy as a candidate for repeal OR renewed justification. The whitelist cannot express the correct move here: the source text is NOT dead. The captured node prose contains substantive supervisory expectations directly on-point to the Mandate — e.g. 'depository institutions should maintain actionable contingency funding plans', a 'cushion of liquid assets', 'stress testing', and that funding strategies must not 'undermine public confidence in the liquidity or stability of subsidiary depository institutions' (O1/O4 relevant). The nothing_in_scope=true / empty-obligations extraction is an EXTRACTION DEFECT, not a substantive dead node. The right action is re-extraction of SR 10-6's obligations (the addendum's contingency-funding-plan duty and the liquidity-cushion expectations) so they can be hooked to O1/O3/O4 — but no whitelist op re-runs extraction or corrects a mis-scoped focus pass, and REPEAL would destroy live guidance that serves the Mandate. Logging as an ADR request: re-extract sr-10-6-liquidity-policy before any repeal/justification decision; do NOT repeal on the strength of an empty-obligation extraction that contradicts the visible source text.

The Board loss-liability to the FDIC (347b-7/OBL-7-9) and the not-insolvent evidence requirement operate as taxpayer-protection/anti-bailout constraints that plausibly function as statutory floors serving O2. A move to soften or remove those (to further advance O1/O3 for critically undercapitalized members) would require weighing an O3-vs-O2 tradeoff the Mandate ranks in O2's favor for that sub-pair, and may breach an inviolable anti-bailout constraint. This is logged as a potential ADR / return-to-Principal rather than proposed as an edit.

M5's residual concern — that O2 currently substitutes for a missing O4 mechanism (see M1) — cannot be cured within this finding via the whitelist: adding an actual O4 self-insurance-substitution facility is a separate design question tracked under M1, not a relation or purpose fix to the §13(3) constraints. No whitelist op here can supply that substitution mechanism; it is logged for the M1 proposal.
